correctness.rationale: The greedy algorithm gives an exact support-width sum over nested rank cuts; the centered-normal decomposition and strict triangle inequality show that every minimum direction is a cut normal. Wheel-matroid 3-connectivity forces λ≥2 away from singleton cuts (Denham et al., Example 2.26). A balanced m-edge λ=2 cut is explicitly constructed for both parities. Comparing two sharp ratios proves all m≥3 and excludes ties. Packaged integer-rank enumeration m=3..9 and direct spanning-tree support tests m=3,4 pass. No finite computation is used to deduce the all-dimensional assertion.

value.rationale: This exact metric invariant of canonical graphic-matroid base polytopes reveals a dimension-dependent qualitative change in globally thinnest supporting directions. The full minimizing-normal classification is needed to understand width-sensitive optimization and polytope geometry; the exact seven-to-eight cutoff is not just a scalar recomputation of known vertex counts. The simple two-branch law follows from a genuinely structural cut-support reduction and an explicit sharp family of 3-separations.
